newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU VETS DISCUSS SWINE FEVER.
newsitem.headline: EU VETS DISCUSS SWINE FEVER.

text.p: The European Union's Standing Veterinary Committee on Wednesday gathered for a special meeting to discuss swine fever after outbreaks in Germany and the Netherlands, a Commission official said.
They were reviewing the situation and discussing possible new measures.
On Tuesday the EU formally imposed a partial ban on the export of pigs from five German Laender (states) and two districts in a sixth because of an outbreak of swine fever.
German authorities have ordered an extensive slaughter programme to contain the highly contagious disease.

Dutch authorities, anxious to prevent restrictions of key pork exports, have decided to slaughter all pigs at 26 farms in the area immediately surrounding the first case -- discovered last Tuesday. An estimated 30,000 are expected to be killed.
The Netherlands exports around 750,000 tonnes of pigs and pork products every year.
On Friday Poland closed its borders to all imports of Dutch pigs, pork and pork products and Belgium said it would tighten frontier checks, although it stopped short of an outright ban.
